gen-comfortaa-gf-ibm-plex-sans-thai-loop: IBM Plex Sans Thai Looped keeps its curves loose and unclosed, a plain sans with quiet manners. Comfortaa up top, round as if drawn with a soft-tipped pen, gives the pair its strongest quality: friendliness without fuss.
gen-comfortaa-gf-noto-sans-shavian: Noto Sans Shavian lays down loose, rope-like curves that never knot. Comfortaa's heading has no calligraphic shading, just smooth tubing, so the body text can be sized up a touch without crowding it.
gen-comfortaa-gf-sarala: A ring-shaped c gives Comfortaa its friendly face. Sarala follows with distinct gaps in its letters and a glassy stroke, so a long read stays approachable and light.
gen-comfortaa-gf-stick: Neon tubing, bent into letters. Comfortaa carries that glow into the heading, while Stick keeps its constant-weight lines and wide exits, so a long passage lets light through every word.
gen-comfortaa-gf-zen-kaku-gothic-antique: Soft rings, stretched out wide. Comfortaa spaces its geometric heading like a loosened spring, and Zen Kaku Gothic Antique tucks in below with a smooth path around every bend and a tidy t.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-taviraj: Blunt, tubular, hard to ignore. Aaargh is built for the loud first line, cut from one gauge of stroke, while Taviraj does the quieter work of a bookish serif, with a restrained difference between stem and joining stroke.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-uchen: Heavy round bowls, stamped with confidence. Aaargh keeps its walls the same thickness all the way around, and Uchen answers with understated thick-thin contrast and curves that welcome the eye.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-cutive: Modern and weightless, letters drifting apart. Arkhip draws every stroke at one thickness, which makes it best for striking headings, while Cutive does its best work in refined, widely tracked running text.
